title: Work-planning words that ended up in runtime data, and now gate play
usableAnswer: A rule we can apply and test. Specifically: (1) may a work-assignment fact ever live in a field the runtime reads, or must every such hold carry an expiry or an owner that can be checked to still exist; (2) for these five requests today, is new people/body/head generation actually closed, or should the hold be dropped and the requests returned to the queue; (3) what the Art Desk should display when a hold refers to an owner that no longer exists — silence, the request as open, or an explicit 'this hold has expired'.
whyItMatters: This is happening right now, measured today. `art/requests/art-desk-reconciliation.json` carries a `holds` map, and five person art requests are held there under the value `d-held-people`: person-production-standing-body, person-production-seated-body, person-child-body-morphology, person-adult-body-silhouette-reexport and person-adult-lectern-pose. `src/authoring/art-desk.ts:304` turns that value into a coverage disposition of "history" with the rendered note "D's hold covers new people/body/head generation. Visible as history, not a P0 generation job." The source of the letter D is `docs/plans/active/alive43-a-art-desk.md:14`, an "Excluded" section listing which lane owned which surface at the time. There is no lane D plan in the repository at all — ALIVE43 has A, L and W. The file landed on 2026-09-15 (253103dd), so for a week a note about who owned what has been reading, to anyone opening the Art Desk, as a standing product decision that new body and head generation is closed. Nobody decided that. It is a fourth species alongside hardcoded names, gated-shut systems and hardcoded decision thresholds: a coordination artefact that became a rule by being written into data.

answer.summary:
A work allocation is not a creative prohibition. Distinguish an explicit owner product restriction (with decision reference), a concrete missing dependency, and a temporary live work lease (owner/checkpoint). They cannot share one unexplained string that hides content as history. Old assignment initials, a missing worker plan or a stale worktree do not justify permanent feature gating.

The queue reports five d-held-people requests hidden by a September 15 allocation. This batch has not independently re-read their current source, so the existing owner verifies the exact current entries before touching them. Generation is not generally closed under current approved art scope. Remove an obsolete assignment hold when confirmed, reconcile each request against already delivered/currently needed work, then return needed work to its real queue; delete genuinely obsolete duplicate requests by existing policy. Do not resurrect completed work or self-approve images. Unknown lease ownership needs explicit coordination, not an automatic product ban or deletion of active work.

Apply the same distinction to 'awaiting researched coefficient' after DEPTH1: an adjustable labelled private assumption is now authorized inside settled behavior. The historical lack of a per-number approval cannot keep the whole system disabled. A true creative hold remains meaningful and must not be released by an expired engineering lease.

Acceptance ChatGPT requests (not executed): Expired/missing assignment owner is distinguishable from a current owner restriction and an actual dependency. Current completed art is not regenerated; still-needed requests are visible. No change to exact human review decisions.
